name: Acute Laryngitis
description: Acute inflammation or irritation of the larynx and vocal folds, commonly associated with a viral upper respiratory infection. The characteristic feature is an acute change in voice such as hoarseness or temporary loss of voice.
associated_symptoms: Runny or blocked nose when associated with a viral infection
physical_examination: Assessment for stridor or respiratory distress
Assessment for cervical or neck abnormalities when symptoms persist
recommended_investigations: Clinical history and examination for uncomplicated acute presentations
Laryngoscopic examination for persistent hoarseness or concerning features
ENT assessment when symptoms persist or structural disease is suspected
contraindications: Persistent hoarseness or red-flag symptoms should not be managed as uncomplicated self-limited laryngitis without further evaluation.

clinical_references.title: Hoarseness
clinical_references.organization: National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders
